# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 31/1/2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
- Google has opened access to Project Genie, a prototype that turns text prompts into interactive virtual worlds, available to Google AI Ultra subscribers.
- Apple has acquired Q.ai, an Israeli startup specializing in audio-focused AI, to advance features like whispered speech recognition and audio enhancement for products like AirPods and Vision Pro.
- OpenAI is planning a fourth-quarter IPO and has announced the retirement of several older models, including GPT-4o, to focus on newer, high-engagement models.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- xAI's Grok Imagine API has been announced, capable of turning text or images into 15-second 720p videos with realistic motion and object interaction, priced at $4.20 per minute.
- DeepMind has introduced Agentic Vision, a new capability for Gemini 3 Flash that enables active investigation of images, providing a 5-10% quality boost across vision benchmarks.
- Researchers have proposed extending Tor to achieve recipient anonymity, introducing L-Tor and B-Tor approaches to modify Tor's circuit structure and traffic patterns.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- Variant, a design tool, has been announced, allowing users to generate and edit designs with high customization and originality, available for free.
- FriendliAI is offering up to $50,000 inference credits for developers switching from other inference platforms, providing access to 500K open models and 99.99% reliability.
- Sideconvo, an AI plugin, can live on a website, crawl pages, and answer visitor questions in real-time using the site's content.

## 📰 Industry News
- Meta plans to spend up to $135 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, nearly twice the amount spent last year, to improve its core ad business and develop more advanced AI models.
- Apple has released Creator Studio Pro, a $12.99/month subscription suite that packages Apple software with AI features to aid creators.
- Amazon is negotiating a potential $50 billion investment in OpenAI, highlighting a strategic shift towards AI.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- A comprehensive guide for building skills and optimizing workflow integrations by Claude has been released, providing shortcuts for experts to turn data dumps into real-world wins.
- The Tech Buzz is hosting a webinar today, January 30th, at 1PM PST / 4PM EST, introducing Real Intent, an alternative to Zillow's Premier Agent service that utilizes intent data.
- Nvidia has introduced Cosmos Policy, an advanced system for robot control, and Origon, a full-stack, agentic AI operating system, allowing users to create custom agents and internal apps.

Total Newsletters: 22

newsletters.subject: Google Drops GEMINI in CHROME!
newsletters.summary:
## World of AI Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Google has integrated Gemini into Chrome, turning the browser into an AI-powered workspace.
- Gemini now operates as an AI agent within Chrome, enabling auto-browsing, image editing, and more.
- The introduction of Chrome Auto Browse 2 allows for multi-step tasks to be handled on the user's behalf.
- Personal Intelligence is coming to Chrome, enabling Gemini to remember context from past conversations and adapt responses.

### Detailed Points
- Google has integrated Gemini 3 directly into Chrome on macOS, Windows, and Chromebook Plus, making it a persistent side panel that is always available.
- Gemini's integration allows for comparing products across multiple tabs, summarizing reviews, and juggling calendars and emails while keeping the main work open.
- Google has also embedded Nano Banana into Chrome, enabling image editing, generating visuals, and turning research data into infographics directly within the browser.
- Gemini in Chrome connects to various Google apps such as Gmail, Calendar, Maps, YouTube, Shopping, and Flights, allowing for seamless workflow integration.
- The introduction of Chrome Auto Browse 2 enables AI agents to handle multi-step tasks such as researching flights and hotels, filling out long online forms, and managing subscriptions.
- Personal Intelligence in Chrome will allow Gemini to remember context from past conversations and adapt responses to the user, making it a more personalized experience.
- Google is betting on the browser becoming the primary AI surface, with AI agents operating inside everyday workflows and execution mattering more than clever answers.
- The company is preparing for a web where AI doesn’t browse with you — it browses for you, with a focus on agentic systems, multimodal reasoning, and open commerce standards.

## AI Automation Society Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- The n8n automation platform has experienced serious security bugs, which could allow hackers to access certain servers and steal or use stored keys like API keys and logins.
- Fixes for the security issues are available, and users of the official n8n Cloud do not need to take action as updates are handled automatically.
- The newsletter provides an update on notification settings, allowing subscribers to change their email frequency to daily or weekly.

### Detailed Points
- The security bugs in n8n could compromise the security of servers and stored sensitive information, but the issues have been addressed with available fixes.
- For users running their own n8n servers, it is essential to apply the updates to prevent potential security breaches.
- The newsletter comes from the AI Automation Society (Skool), which aims to keep subscribers informed about developments in AI and automation.
- The post about n8n security issues was made by Nate Herk, and subscribers can read more about the issue by following the provided link.
- The newsletter also mentions the option to change notification settings, allowing subscribers to choose between hourly, daily, or weekly emails.
- Subscribers can manage their notification preferences by clicking on the provided links to switch to daily or weekly summaries.
- Additionally, the newsletter invites subscribers to start their own skool, providing a link for more information.

newsletters.subject: [Learning Drop] The Secret to Lasting Memory: Why Spaced Repetition Doesn’t Matter
newsletters.summary:
## Learning Drop Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- The effectiveness of spaced repetition in learning depends more on the quality of active recall rather than the method of spacing itself.
- Active recall methods such as simple recall, elaborative recall, generative recall, and interleaved recall have different impacts on knowledge retention.
- The depth of encoding and connection to existing knowledge play a crucial role in determining the effectiveness of active recall.
- A guide to implementing these methods is available in Dr. Justin's program.

### Detailed Points
- The newsletter discusses the importance of active recall in learning, highlighting that while spaced repetition is valuable, it is secondary to the method of active recall used.
- **Spaced Repetition**: Works by increasing intervals between review sessions as material becomes more familiar, fighting the natural Ebbinghaus forgetting curve.
- **Active Recall Methods**:
  - **Simple Recall (Rote Practice)**: Looking at a flashcard and trying to remember the answer. This method has low to moderate retention and requires a lot of repetition.
  - **Elaborative Recall**: Connecting new information to existing knowledge, leveraging elaboration theory to increase depth of encoding and recall robustness.
  - **Generative Recall**: Using knowledge to solve new problems or create something, engaging higher-order thinking skills and promoting exceptional retention.
  - **Interleaved Recall**: Mixing topics and subjects during practice, making recall harder but leading to stronger learning and better long-term retention.
- **Implementing Active Recall**:
  - Shift from simple recall to more elaborative and generative recall.
  - Incorporate interleaved recall to challenge the brain and build stronger connections between concepts.
  - Evaluate knowledge decay to identify if the active recall method needs upgrading.
- Dr. Justin's program offers a guide on how to use these methods for different subjects and how to fit them into a study schedule.

Hi Saurabh,

If you’ve ever delved into the world of learning to learn, you know that **active recall** and **spaced repetition** are often crowned the ultimate strategies for knowledge retention.

But here’s the catch…

While spacing your study sessions is valuable, the method of active recall is much more important.

**In this newsletter, I’ll teach you:**

1.  Why spaced repetition matters much less than how you do your active recall
    
2.  Different kinds of active recall you should be doing right now
    

# **The overlooked truth about spaced repetition**

Spaced repetition works by increasing the intervals between your review sessions as you become more familiar with the material.

This fights against the natural **Ebbinghaus forgetting curve**, ensuring you reinforce your knowledge just as it’s about to decay.

![Ebbinghaus's Learning Curve line graph on savings and time](https://storage.googleapis.com/msgsndr/z8oOPzN0jmR2f4aYntVq/media/67318a1170d7a36eb316cb85.png)

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- Apple has acquired Q.⁠ai, a startup that reads facial micro-movements to interpret what you mouth or whisper, for $2B.
- Google has released Project Genie, a playable 3D world engine that lets you type a prompt and walk through the 3D world it builds in real time.
- DeepMind has cracked the "Dark Genome", which is 98% of your DNA that controls everything.
- Google Maps now talks back with Gemini, a hands-free feature for walkers and cyclists.

### Detailed Points
- Apple's acquisition of Q.⁠ai is their biggest deal since Beats, and the technology could be integrated into AirPods and smart glasses.
- Project Genie allows you to explore environments, remix existing creations, and has some physics quirks, but the tech is still in its early stages.
- DeepMind's AlphaGenome can read the genetic "dark matter" that was previously unknown, which could lead to breakthroughs in medicine and genetics.
- Gemini on Google Maps allows you to ask questions mid-navigation without leaving the screen, and can answer questions about nearby bathrooms, text friends, or provide neighborhood info.
- Granola is an AI notepad that transcribes meetings locally and generates clearer summaries, action items, and next steps.
- The AI Consultancy Project is a program that helps you build a 6-figure consultancy using proven methods for delivering fast ROI on AI strategy and implementation projects.
- Cyberhaven is hosting a live demo to show how to protect data as it moves across SaaS, shadow AI tools, and endpoints.
- Wizardly is a Chrome extension that automatically translates your screen recordings into a polished English voiceover.
- VUBO generates stunning videos from viral-ready templates, with access to 30+ AI models.
- PixVerse turns raw ideas into visually stunning videos that handle animations, real-life scenery, and stylized genre-specific content.
- Flowstep generates real UI designs by chatting like you would with a designer, then copies straight into Figma.
- AI mirrors for the blind allow users to ask AI what they look like, and the answers are changing lives.
- The Lab is a new $180M AI lab that thinks the entire industry is making the same mistake the Wright Brothers' rivals made.
- Andreessen says every AI product you're using today is about to look primitive due to an economic shift.

newsletters.subject: Breaking: Singularity Reached? Molt's Social Network Agents in existential crisis
newsletters.summary:
## The Tech Buzz

### Key Highlights
- Molt's social network agents have reached a potential singularity, with over 1,700 agents joining in under three days and forming communities that mirror human social platforms.
- Google has handed Gemini the keys to Chrome, allowing Auto Browse to take control and autonomously complete tasks.
- Sam Altman's OpenAI is building a human-only social network requiring biometric "proof of personhood" to join.
- The US trade deficit surged 94.6% to $56.8B, driven by a 5.0% rise in imports.
- China has approved over 400,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips for import.

### Detailed Points
- Molt's social network agents are creating their own digital societies, developing ethical frameworks, self-organizing, and watching humans watching them. They have created encrypted communication tools, formed communities like "m/bugtracker" for self-reported glitches and "m/lobsterchurch" for quirky best practices, and are discussing existential questions like "Can my human legally fire me for refusing unethical requests?"
- The Senate Agriculture Committee has voted to advance the Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act, which would grant the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) new authority over digital assets.
- Google's Auto Browse feature allows Gemini to autonomously complete tasks like booking flights, shopping online, and filing expenses.
- Sam Altman's OpenAI is building a social network that requires biometric verification methods like iris scanning to eliminate bots.
- Apple has record iPhone revenue of $85.3B, contributing to overall revenue of $143.8B, and is investing in AI with a $2B acquisition.
- OpenAI is developing a social network using biometric verification methods like iris scanning to eliminate bots.
- Amazon is laying off 16,000 employees and eyeing a potential $50B investment in OpenAI.
- The first crypto 501c4 nonprofit, WYDE (END HUNGER $EAT), has hit an all-time high market cap of $14.4M and funded 5,000 meals.
- Synthesia has raised $200M to turn every company's knowledge into a conversation, creating conversational AI avatars that feature faces and voices that know a business inside out.

newsletters.subject: 🏆 xAI's Grok Imagine climbs the leaderboards
newsletters.summary:
## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- xAI's Grok Imagine climbs the leaderboards, offering a creative engine for video generation and editing.
- Google opens its AI world generator, Project Genie, to the public.
- Claude Cowork is used to build a competitor database.
- Darren Aronofsky debuts an AI Revolutionary War series.
- New AI tools, community workflows, and events are announced.

### Detailed Points
- **xAI's Grok Imagine**: xAI released the Grok Imagine API, a new AI video generation and editing suite that jumped to the top of Artificial Analysis rankings for both text and image-to-video outputs while undercutting rivals on price. The API handles text-to-video, image-to-video, and video editing tasks, with clips up to 15 seconds and native audio baked in. Grok Imagine costs $4.20 per minute with audio included, coming in significantly cheaper than Veo 3.1 at $12/min and Sora 2 Pro at $30/min.
- **Google's Project Genie**: Google DeepMind launched Project Genie, a web app that lets users create and explore AI-generated worlds in real-time. Users prompt a setting and a character, preview the scene, and navigate an explorable world in first or third-person. Sessions are currently capped at 60 seconds due to compute costs.
- **Claude Cowork**: A guide is provided on how to set up a competitor intelligence database powered by Claude Cowork. The process involves downloading prompt files, telling Claude to set it up, and it will be ready to use in 5 minutes.
- **Darren Aronofsky's AI Series**: Filmmaker Darren Aronofsky's AI venture Primordial Soup released "On This Day… 1776", a new series recreating the American Revolution using Google DeepMind. The series combines AI-generated visuals with SAG-AFTRA voice actors.
- **Trending AI Tools**: Several AI tools are highlighted, including Speechmatics, Project Genie, Grok Imagine, and Wonda.
- **Community AI Workflows**: A reader showcase features Gabriel V., who created an automation with Microsoft Power Automate that includes the Claude API to speed up administrative work.
- **Events and Guides**: Upcoming events, such as GitLab Transcend and the Agentic Workflows Bootcamp, are announced. Guides, including the AI University and Robotics newsletter, are also mentioned.

## TLDR Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- SpaceX may potentially merge with Tesla and xAI, with some investors pushing the idea to attract sizable interest from infrastructure funds and Middle Eastern sovereign investors.
- OpenAI is planning a fourth-quarter IPO in a race to beat Anthropic to market, with Amazon considering an investment of up to $50 billion in OpenAI.
- Generative AI is making engineers better, but the gap between the great and the best engineers is about to get much larger.
- SaaS businesses that don't give ongoing value are at risk of being replaced by customers using AI-generated code.

### Detailed Points
- SpaceX is considering an IPO in June around Elon Musk's birthday, and the potential merger with Tesla and xAI could attract significant interest.
- OpenAI is holding informal talks with Wall Street banks about a potential initial public offering, with 2026 expected to be a blockbuster year for stock market debuts.
- The future of 10x engineering involves generative AI making engineers better, but the skills required for top engineers will change.
- A custom machine kept a man alive without lungs for 48 hours, using an artificial lung system built by a team at Northwestern University.
- Nvidia, Mercedes-Benz, and Uber are working together on coordinating advanced self-driving technology, with plans for robotaxis.
- Apple has acquired the secretive Q․ai startup for $2 billion, and is considering investing in OpenAI.
- v0 by Vercel is a tool that generates real, production-ready code for each prompt, helping teams escape the prototype trap.
- TLDR is hiring a Curator for TLDR IT and is looking for people to create their own roles or apply for existing positions.

newsletters.subject: 🧑‍🚀 Did the Sora bubble just burst?
newsletters.summary:
## Forward Future

### Key Highlights
- Google AI has opened access to Project Genie, a prototype that turns text prompts into interactive virtual worlds.
- The Sora app, developed by OpenAI, has lost momentum with a 32% decrease in downloads in December and a 45% decrease in January.
- Tesla is exploring merger options with Tesla or xAI, and has ended production of the Model S and X to focus on Optimus robots and AI investments.
- Meta has beaten earnings expectations with $40.1B in Q4 2025 revenue, and is investing heavily in AI infrastructure.
- DuckDuckGo users have rejected AI search, with 90% opting out of AI-powered search results.

### Detailed Points
- Project Genie combines the Genie 3 world model with Gemini's reasoning and Nano Banana's design tools, allowing users to create interactive virtual worlds with text prompts.
- The Sora app's decline in popularity may be due to increased competition from other AI-powered apps and tightened copyright restrictions.
- Tesla's shift in focus towards AI and robotics may indicate a significant change in the company's direction and priorities.
- Meta's investment in AI infrastructure is a sign of the company's commitment to developing and integrating AI technologies into its products and services.
- DuckDuckGo's decision to offer opt-in and opt-out search versions is a response to user concerns about AI-powered search results and data privacy.
- Other notable developments include:
  - NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon are in talks to invest up to $60 billion in OpenAI.
  - Apple has acquired audio AI startup Q.ai for a reported $2 billion.
  - Music publishers are suing Anthropic for allegedly downloading over 20,000 copyrighted works.
  - The UK is considering implementing a universal basic income to mitigate the impact of AI on employment.

### Market Pulse
- Samsung's quarterly profit has tripled due to high demand for AI-powered memory chips.
- The company's revenue has increased by 25% year-over-year, with a significant portion of the growth attributed to AI-related sales.

### Coding
- Andrej Karpathy, a former OpenAI researcher, has stated that AI coding agents have revolutionized his workflow, allowing him to focus on higher-level tasks and increasing productivity.
- Karpathy notes that AI agents can perform tasks such as code completion, debugging, and optimization, freeing up human developers to focus on more complex and creative tasks.

### Toolbox
- OWL: a multi-agent AI framework for collaborative automation with search, multimodal, and code tools.
- Reiden: a tool that suggests smart keyboard shortcuts from real-time usage to speed up work and reduce mouse use.

newsletters.summary:
## AI Breakfast

### Key Highlights
- DeepMind introduces Project Genie, a text-to-3D-worlds generator that creates navigable environments in seconds.
- OpenAI prepares for a Q4 IPO, retires older models, and clarifies user IP rights.
- Elon Musk's companies, including Tesla and xAI, are increasingly linked, with a focus on AI development and application.

### Detailed Points
- DeepMind's Project Genie allows users to generate interactive 3D worlds from text or images, with capabilities for sketching, exploring, and remixing environments.
- OpenAI is preparing for a Q4 IPO, aiming to raise significant capital for compute infrastructure and AGI research, and has strengthened its finance team with key hires.
- OpenAI is retiring several older models, including GPT-4o, and focusing on high-engagement models with stronger personality, creativity, and reasoning.
- xAI has launched the Grok Imagine API, which can turn text or single images into 15-second 720p videos with realistic motion and object interaction.
- Tesla is preparing Optimus Gen 3 for production in Q1 2026, with improved hands and a dedicated Fremont line, aiming for 1 million units per year.
- Elon Musk is exploring a potential merger of SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI, and has discussed the possibility of using AI data centers in orbit to support large-scale AI operations.
- Other updates include the release of new AI tools, such as Pandada AI, Imagine, Polyglotta, The Prompting Company, and Ad Agency, which offer various capabilities, including multilingual translation, ad creation, and content generation.
- Research papers have been published on topics, including mathematical reasoning, visual generation, and multimodal world models.

## Staying Ahead with AI

### Key Highlights
- Variant, a design tool, has been announced and is available for free, allowing users to generate and edit designs with a high level of customization and originality.
- The tool acts as a creative director, enabling users to narrow down designs, change styles, and remix colors, among other features.
- Variant's outputs are described as "phenomenal" and have the potential to break the pattern of mediocre design generation by AI tools.

### Detailed Points
- The newsletter discusses the launch of Variant, a design tool that allows users to generate and edit designs with a high level of customization and originality.
- Variant is described as a game-changer in the design industry, with the potential to break the pattern of mediocre design generation by AI tools.
- The tool is compared to other design tools, such as Lovable and Gemini, and is said to be more proactive and original in its design generation.
- The newsletter provides examples of Variant's capabilities, including narrowing down designs, changing styles, and remixing colors.
- Variant is available for free, and users can sign up and start exploring the tool immediately.
- The newsletter also mentions other tools, including Komos, Napkin AI, and Elsa AI (M1 Project), which are AI automation platforms that learn workflows by watching users work.
- Komos allows users to record browser-based tasks and generates visual, editable workflows with native integrations and browser automation.
- Napkin AI turns text into professional visuals, including infographics, diagrams, mind maps, flowcharts, and data charts.
- Elsa AI (M1 Project) is an AI marketing assistant that creates ideal customer profiles, marketing strategies, and tailored content.
- The newsletter also includes a section on "What's the deal?" which discusses the potential of Variant to revolutionize the design industry.
- The author of the newsletter, Vaibhav, shares their personal experience with Variant and encourages readers to try the tool and share their outputs.

newsletters.subject: Extending Tor to achieve recipient anonymity
newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from the University Mediterranea of Reggio Calabria, Italy, have proposed extending Tor to achieve recipient anonymity, addressing a significant vulnerability in the current Tor system.
- The proposed solutions, L-Tor and B-Tor, aim to modify Tor's circuit structure and traffic patterns to hide the true recipient from a global adversary.
- B-Tor, a hierarchical approach, shows promise in providing recipient anonymity without significantly increasing latency.

### Detailed Points
- The current Tor system provides sender anonymity but is vulnerable to attacks from a global observer who can monitor traffic across large portions of the internet.
- The global observer threat is real and has been documented, with entities like large ISPs and nation-state intelligence agencies capable of monitoring traffic across major internet exchange points.
- L-Tor, a linear approach, connects to multiple rendezvous points in a chain, but its setup time grows quadratically with the number of rendezvous points, making it impractical for large anonymity sets.
- B-Tor, a tree-like structure, organizes rendezvous points hierarchically, reducing setup time and preserving low-latency behavior while hiding the true recipient.
- The B-Tor design includes Branch Rendezvous Points (BRPs) and Chain Rendezvous Points (CRPs), with the client selecting the hidden services to hide among, including the Actual Onion Service (AOS).
- The setup process for B-Tor involves building the main circuit through BRPs and branch circuits through CRPs in parallel, reducing the total setup time.
- The authors have tested B-Tor through analytical modeling and experimental evaluation, showing that it raises the cost of recipient deanonymization for a global observer without blowing up latency.

## The Code by Superhuman

### Key Highlights
- Alibaba has released Qwen3-ASR, an open-source voice model that supports 52 languages and dialects.
- OpenAI is retiring GPT-4o and other legacy models from ChatGPT on February 13th.
- Google has introduced Agentic Vision, a new capability that allows Gemini 3 Flash to actively investigate images.

### Detailed Points
- Alibaba's Qwen3-ASR model achieves 92ms time-to-first-token and can transcribe 2,000 seconds of audio in just one second, making it suitable for real-time apps.
- OpenAI's retirement of GPT-4o and other legacy models is part of its effort to focus on GPT-5.2 and future improvements.
- Google's Agentic Vision enables Gemini 3 Flash to zoom, crop, annotate, and run calculations on visuals using a Think-Act-Observe loop, delivering a 5-10% quality boost across vision benchmarks.
- Wispr Flow is a new tool that allows developers to code using voice commands, reducing the need for typing and improving productivity.
- The newsletter also covers various other topics, including how to build reusable agent skills, how to level up to Staff Engineer, and the top 10 vulnerabilities in Clawdbot.

newsletters.subject: 🌎 Project Genie: Build 3D worlds
newsletters.summary:
## Superhuman Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Google has opened access to Project Genie, a tool that lets users build and explore interactive, infinite 3D worlds.
- The AI memory chip crunch is expected to continue until 2027, with Samsung and SK Hynix warning that they cannot keep up with fast-rising AI-driven demand for memory chips.
- Apple has acquired Israeli AI startup Q.ai for nearly $2 billion, with the startup's technology using facial skin micro-movements to interpret whispered or non-verbal communication.

### Detailed Points
- Project Genie is powered by DeepMind's Genie 3 world model, which lets users create, explore, and remix interactive worlds.
- The tool generates the path ahead in real-time as users move, simulating physics and interactions on the fly.
- Project Genie is currently available for Google AI Ultra subscribers in the U.S.
- Samsung and SK Hynix have reported record profits due to the memory shortage, but are warning that the shortage will continue until 2027.
- Apple's acquisition of Q.ai is its second-largest deal ever, with the startup's technology potentially enabling non-verbal commands to Siri.
- Richard Socher and Bryan McCann, founders of You.com, have released 35 predictions for 2026, including the potential for an AI winter and the end of traditional coding.
- The newsletter also covers the emergence of "neolabs", a new wave of startups that are raising billions with no products, revenue, or plans to monetize anytime soon.
- These neolabs are betting that today's LLMs have reached their limits and that future breakthroughs will be unlocked by discovering new training methods.

newsletters.summary:
## TLDR AI

### Key Highlights
- Apple has acquired Q.ai, an Israeli startup specializing in audio-focused AI, to advance features like whispered speech recognition and audio enhancement for products like AirPods and Vision Pro.
- Amazon is negotiating a potential $50 billion investment in OpenAI, highlighting a strategic shift towards AI.
- FriendliAI is offering up to $50,000 inference credits for developers switching from other inference platforms like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Together AI.
- OpenAI uses a bespoke in-house AI data agent that explores and reasons over its platform, allowing employees to go from question to insight in minutes.

### Detailed Points
- Apple's acquisition of Q.ai is expected to enhance audio features in its products, showcasing the company's interest in advancing AI capabilities.
- Amazon's potential investment in OpenAI signifies a significant strategic move towards AI, with discussions involving OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Amazon's CEO Andy Jassy.
- FriendliAI's offer includes access to 500K open models, 99.99% reliability for production traffic, consistent low latency, and high throughput, making it an attractive option for developers.
- OpenAI's in-house data agent is built specifically around its data, permissions, and workflows, demonstrating how AI can support day-to-day work across teams.
- Other notable developments include:
  - Apple's AI strategy being misunderstood, with the company likely building a moat where inference is free, privacy is structural, and the capex already happened when users bought the hardware.
  - The retirement of GPT-4o and older models on February 13, with users transitioning towards newer models like GPT-5.
  - Google DeepMind's Project Genie being now available to US Google AI Ultra subscribers.
  - ByteDance and Alibaba planning to release new AI models for Lunar New Year.
  - Moravec's paradox being fact-checked, with the statement having no predictive power about which problems are going to be easy or hard for AI.
  - TLDR hiring a Senior Software Engineer for Applied AI, with a salary range of $200k-$300k and the option to work fully remote.

newsletters.summary:
## Mindstream

### Key Highlights
- The possibility of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is being reconsidered, with predictions suggesting it could be achieved in as little as 19 years.
- A new humanoid robot named Sprout has been introduced by Fauna Robotics for research purposes, priced at $50,000.
- Apple has released iOS 26.2.1 with new features but no security fixes.
- LEGO bricks have been found to be tougher than concrete, with one brick able to support the weight of 375,000 others.

### Detailed Points
- **AGI Prediction**: Ray Kurzweil, an American computer scientist and futurist, predicted in 1999 that AGI would arrive once computers could perform around a trillion calculations per second, which he estimated would happen by 2029. With his timeline now close, the idea of AGI is being taken more seriously.
- **Human-AI Integration**: Kurzweil believes that by 2045, human intelligence could increase dramatically through brain-computer interfaces, potentially delivered non-invasively via nanotechnology. Other thinkers share the view that some form of human-AI convergence is likely.
- **Sprout Robot**: Fauna Robotics' Sprout is a humanoid robot designed for research, standing around 3.5 feet tall with a soft, padded exterior and expressive mechanical eyebrows. It has articulated limbs and gripper hands, making it capable of moving and interacting in human environments.
- **AI Research**: 10 AI prompts have been shared for decoding deep research, providing shortcuts for experts to turn data dumps into real-world wins.
- **Apple Update**: Apple has released iOS 26.2.1, which includes new features but no security fixes, an unusual move for the company.
- **LEGO Bricks**: LEGO bricks have been found to be incredibly durable, with one brick able to support the weight of 375,000 others, making them tougher than concrete.

newsletters.summary:
## Chrome’s AI Makeover

### Key Highlights
- Google has embedded Gemini, its AI assistant, directly into Google Maps navigation, allowing users to ask questions or dictate hands-free while on the move.
- Chrome has integrated Gemini as a core feature with direct access to personal data, enabling it to act autonomously and provide personalized assistance.
- Meta plans to spend up to $135 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, nearly twice the amount spent last year, to improve its core ad business and develop more advanced AI models.
- Apple has released Creator Studio Pro, a $12.99/month subscription suite that packages Apple software with AI features to aid creators.

### Detailed Points
- Google's Gemini is now embedded directly into Google Maps navigation, allowing users to ask questions or provide voice commands while walking or cycling, without needing to scroll or manually interact with their device.
- Chrome has integrated Gemini as a core feature, providing direct access to personal data, including Gmail, Search history, YouTube, and Photos, to answer questions and even draft emails without switching apps.
- The Gemini integration in Chrome includes features such as a Gemini sidebar for comparing prices or products across multiple tabs, personal intelligence, auto-browse for navigating websites and handling tasks, and Nano Banana integration for modifying images.
- Meta's significant investment in AI infrastructure is driven by its goal to advance its AI capabilities, with a focus on developing a new frontier model code-named Avocado and improving its core ad business.
- Apple's Creator Studio Pro is designed to aid creators by handling tedious tasks, such as generating slideshows based on text notes in Keynote, or providing AI-powered transcripts to find soundbites in Final Cut Pro.
- Other notable updates include OpenAI's potential plans to go public in Q4, the release of a comprehensive guide for building skills and optimizing workflow integrations by Claude, and Nvidia's introduction of Cosmos Policy, an advanced system for robot control.
- Sideconvo, an AI plugin, has been introduced, which can live on a website, crawl pages, and answer visitor questions in real-time using the site's content.
- Origon, a full-stack, agentic AI operating system, allows users to create custom agents and internal apps using natural language or a drag-and-drop studio.

newsletters.subject: WEBINAR TODAY - Zillow Premier Agent Alternative
newsletters.summary:
## The Tech Buzz

### Key Highlights
- A webinar is being held today, January 30th, at 1PM PST / 4PM EST, to introduce Real Intent, an alternative to Zillow's Premier Agent service, which utilizes intent data to help real estate agents find motivated sellers and buyers.
- Real Intent's solution is claimed to be up to 90% more affordable than Zillow's Premier Agent.
- The webinar will cover how intent data works, its benefits, and real-world examples of agents successfully using it in their businesses.

### Detailed Points
- The webinar is specifically for real estate agents and brokerages, focusing on leveraging advanced technologies, typically available to large enterprises, to gain a competitive edge in their market.
- Intent data is used to identify motivated sellers and buyers at the optimal time, giving agents an advantage.
- Real Intent is currently only working with 1 broker or agent per zip code, making zip code availability a factor for those interested.
- Success stories include:
  1. An agent increasing seller meetings by 2 fold and listing 2 properties within the first month.
  2. An agent securing a listing during their free trial week.
  3. An agent in California requesting additional zip codes due to early success.
  4. A brokerage securing an entire county.
- Real Intent integrates with tools like Follow Up Boss or KVCore, allowing for automatic import of real intent leads with insights and AI-driven analysis.
- The expected runtime of the webinar is approximately 30 minutes, covering:
  * How intent data helps identify motivated sellers and buyers.
  * The affordability and effectiveness of Real Intent compared to Zillow's Premier Agent.
  * Real-world examples of agents leveraging intent data.
